response.answer: Your record says you favor written-statements-first for contested mediations because it exposes the actual points of disagreement before a meeting, limits re-litigation of history, and can make settlement cleaner. You describe settled matters as suitable for live check-ins, while contested matters should be written first; you also make an exception for true crises, which need an immediate room. The two-day lead time is documented and affordable under the service agreement. Your experience includes an all-live February mediation escalating badly without written positions, whereas the team-merger mediation settled cleanly after statements identified only two real issues. Reorganization-driven mediation volume makes that format choice more consequential. Evidence boundary: this reflects your recorded rationale, not an independent assessment of every request.
